page: Amazon Web Services m6in.8xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features 32 virtual CPUs and 16 physical cores based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Network connectivity is a key feature, delivering a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the m6in.8xlarge in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core Geekbench score of 1654.0 and a multi-core score of 13933.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 36724.04. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only large block bandwidth of 150.47 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 68.25 GB/sec. In database operations, the instance handles 31.22 million Redis SET operations per second. For language model workloads, the instance processes prompts at 64.08 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model, though performance drops to a weak 6.22 tokens per second on a larger 70B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m6in.8xlarge offers a balanced resource profile for network-heavy workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The combination of 50 Gbps network bandwidth and dedicated Intel Xeon processing power makes it suitable for mid-sized databases, static web serving, enterprise application hosting, and moderate data processing tasks. However, the lack of local storage and GPU accelerators makes it less suitable for high-performance storage-bound databases or large-scale deep learning training.
